cues.en: Simple question. Which of these items is the healthiest?
cues.zh: 简单问一下，这几样东西里哪样最健康？

cues.en: Is it this salad,
cues.zh: 是这份沙拉，

cues.en: this bracelet,
cues.zh: 这条手链，

cues.en: this eye mask, or this badge necklace thing?
cues.zh: 这个眼罩，还是这个徽章项链之类的东西？

cues.en: Well, thanks to science, I can now use my health o meter to see which of these releases the most healthy particles.
cues.zh: 多亏了科学，现在我可以用健康测量仪看看哪样东西释放的健康粒子最多。

cues.en: First, the salad.
cues.zh: 先测沙拉。

cues.en: Nothing
cues.zh: 什么都没有。

cues.en: really here. That's odd. And the bracelet?
cues.zh: 这里几乎测不到。真奇怪。那手链呢？

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: Getting a little better. Starting to detect some health particles now. How about the eye mask?
cues.zh: 好一些了。现在能测到一些健康粒子了。眼罩怎么样？

cues.en: Now we're cooking with gas.
cues.zh: 这下渐入佳境了。

cues.en: And finally, the badge thing.
cues.zh: 最后，是这个胸牌一样的东西。

cues.en: Ladies and gentlemen, we have a winner. Wait. This isn't my health o meter. Somebody seems to have switched it for a Geiger counter.
cues.zh: 女士们先生们，胜出者诞生了。等等，这不是我的健康测量仪，好像有人把它换成了盖革计数器。

cues.en: That's right, folks. These so called wellness products, which all purport to do everything from boost your mood to cure your diseases and boost your health,
cues.zh: 没错，各位。这些所谓的养生产品，号称能搞定一切——从改善心情到包治百病，再到增进健康，

cues.en: are actually fairly radioactive.
cues.zh: 其实辐射都相当大。

cues.en: All of these items are sold as negative ion products, which are claimed to produce negative and be good for you. This isn't even the first time we've talked about these either. Last year I made a video deep diving into these quack medicine nonsense products and did a series of tests to not only show that they're radioactive,
cues.zh: 这些商品都是以“负离子产品”的名义销售的，号称能产生负离子并对身体有益。我们甚至都不是第一次聊这个话题了。去年我就做过一期视频，深入扒了扒这些江湖骗术的扯淡产品，并做了一系列测试，不仅证明了它们具有放射性，

cues.en: but determine exactly what radioactive element was inside of them. Last time we talked about these bracelets and pendants and several items, and I wanna quickly review those findings before we talk about some amazing updates and these new products that I found recently.
cues.zh: 还查清了里面究竟含有哪种放射性元素。上次我们聊了这些手串、吊坠等好几款产品，在聊最近发现的新产品和一些惊人进展之前，我想先带大家快速回顾一下当时的发现。

cues.en: So to review, last time we did four tests.
cues.zh: 回顾一下，上次我们做了四项测试。

cues.en: First, we measured the items with a Geiger counter to get an idea of how radioactive they are. Then we used a device called a cloud chamber to actually see the radioactive particles coming off of them.
cues.zh: 首先，我们用盖革计数器测量了这些物品，了解它们的放射性水平。然后，我们用一种叫云室的设备，实际看到了从中释放的放射性粒子。

cues.en: These tests alone were pretty damning, but I wanted to know exactly what was in them. To do that, I used gamma spectroscopy and measured the spectrum of gamma rays coming off the items.
cues.zh: 仅这些测试就已经很有说服力了，但我想确切知道里面到底是什么。为此，我使用了伽马能谱法，测量了这些物品释放的伽马射线光谱。

cues.en: As a quick refresher, gamma rays are just very high energy rays of light that come from the decay of radioactive elements.
cues.zh: 简单回顾一下，伽马射线就是放射性元素衰变产生的高能光线。

cues.en: Each element will release gamma rays at specific wavelengths.
cues.zh: 每种元素会在特定波长释放伽马射线。

cues.en: So by measuring the spectrum, it's very easy to tell what's in the sample.
cues.zh: 所以只要测量光谱，就很容易判断样本里有什么。

cues.en: In this case, it turned out to be thorium,
cues.zh: 在这个例子里，结果是钍，

cues.en: a radioactive element next to uranium on the periodic table. Just to double check this result and confirm it, I sent a bracelet to the fantastic Adam McCombs,
cues.zh: 一种在元素周期表上紧挨着铀的放射性元素。为了复核并确认这个结果，我把一只手链寄给了了不起的 Adam McCombs，

cues.en: who runs an electron microscope lab. He was able to use the microscope to also measure what material was in here and his results matched mine.
cues.zh: 他运营着一间电子显微镜实验室。他用显微镜也测量了里面的材料，结果和我的吻合。

cues.en: Some of the products we looked at last time were truly horrific.
cues.zh: 我们上次看到的某些产品真是糟糕透了。

cues.en: The bracelets are made by just mixing thorium dioxide powder into the plastic as it's made and end up shedding radioactive dust into your environment as you're wearing it. And considering you're meant to wear it all the time, this could well mean breathing in some of that dust.
cues.zh: 这些手镯是在塑料制作过程中，直接把二氧化钍粉末混进去制成的。佩戴时，它们会把放射性粉尘散到周围环境中。考虑到你本该一直戴着它，这很可能意味着你会吸入其中一些粉尘。

cues.en: Worse still was this massager wand, which literally just had a pile of thorium dioxide powder inside, which could be accessed by pulling on the back plug. And the degeneracy didn't stop there. Some of the worst of these were full pieces of clothing or bedsheets,
cues.zh: 更糟的是这款按摩棒，里面竟然就装了一堆二氧化钍粉末，拔下后端的塞子就能接触到。更离谱的还在后面。有些最糟糕的产品是整件衣服或整套床单，

cues.en: all potentially laced with this material.
cues.zh: 都可能掺有这种材料。

cues.en: If you'd like to see a more in-depth analysis, I've linked to the previous video below and in the cards of this video.
cues.zh: 如果你想看更深入的分析，我在下方简介和本视频的卡片中都附上了上一期视频的链接。

cues.en: All of these items use the label negative ion and purport to release so called negative ions which they claim are good for you. When in reality, these products either do nothing or just slowly give you cancer potentially.
cues.zh: 这些产品都打着“负离子”的标签，声称能释放所谓的负离子，并宣称对身体有益。但实际上，它们要么毫无作用，要么可能正在慢慢让你致癌。

cues.en: Now this isn't to be confused with these air ionizers which use electricity to generate those negative ions. But like the bracelets, they're quack nonsense all the same. Sure, they put out negative ions and at least they're not radioactive,
cues.zh: 注意别把这些和用电来产生负离子的空气负离子发生器混为一谈。不过和那些手环一样，它们同样是伪科学智商税。当然，它们确实能释放负离子，而且至少没有放射性，

cues.en: but they also release ozone which is poison.
cues.zh: 但它们同时也会释放臭氧，而臭氧是有毒的。

cues.en: So as a rule, when it comes to products that claim to make you instantly more healthy, you're better off just eating a salad and avoiding all this horseshit entirely.
cues.zh: 所以一般来说，遇到那些声称能让你瞬间更健康的产品，你最好还是老老实实吃份沙拉，彻底避开这些鬼话。

cues.en: Now before I talk about the new and equally horrific items that I found, I wanna give a very exciting update. Since the last video, I was actually contacted by both representatives of Amazon
cues.zh: 在讲我发现的那些同样骇人的新玩意之前，我想先分享一个非常激动人心的进展。上次视频之后，亚马逊的代表和美国核管理委员会都联系了我

cues.en: and the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission about the video and was asked to file a formal complaint with both.
cues.zh: 了解那个视频的情况，并要求我向双方提交正式投诉。

cues.en: As a result, Amazon has now pulled dozens and dozens of these dangerous quack products from their site.
cues.zh: 结果，亚马逊现已从其网站上撤下了几十件这类危险的假药产品。

cues.en: And better still, the NRC has banned the sale of these items in The US, and at least two companies that were making them have been shut down. To say that this is a massive win is an understatement.
cues.zh: 更棒的是，NRC 已禁止这些产品在美国销售，至少两家生产这些产品的公司已被关闭。说这是一场巨大的胜利，都算是轻描淡写了。

cues.en: I honestly never thought that a stupid YouTube video could make such a real impact, but I am thrilled that it did. Now it is so much harder for these quacks to sell their products, and people are much safer for it. But that's not to say the fight is over. The snake oil salesmen that make these products have simply found new ways of marketing their garbage.
cues.zh: 老实说，我从没想过一个愚蠢的 YouTube 视频能产生如此真实的影响，但我很高兴它做到了。现在这些江湖郎中推销产品难多了，人们也因此安全多了。但这并不是说斗争已经结束。生产这些产品的蛇油贩子只是找到了推销他们垃圾的新方法。

cues.en: Instead of negative ion, now they call the products things like quantum energy or scalar energy or similar vague nonsense terms.
cues.zh: 他们现在不再说负离子，而是把产品叫作量子能量、标量能量之类模糊又荒唐的名字。

cues.en: But nonetheless, they are much harder to find. So now let's talk about the new items I found, and then I wanna talk about what to do about them. Now that I know how seriously the NRC takes these issues, it's so much easier to find and report them when they pop up. Now what exactly did I find? Well, you saw them in the intro. The first are these eye masks from a company called Energy Armor.
cues.zh: 不过，这些产品确实更难找了。现在来聊聊我发现的新产品，再谈谈该怎么应对。既然我知道 NRC 对这些问题有多重视，它们一出现，我就更容易找到并举报。那我到底发现了什么？开场时你们已经看到了。第一种是 Energy Armor 公司生产的眼罩。

cues.en: With the bracelets, I saw some people argue that the risk from the dust was minimal, but come on. Strapping these things to your face and gently huffing the dust all night or getting it in your eyes, that can't possibly be good. I ran the exact same test as last time, first checking with a Geiger counter and then using my gamma spectrometer to determine the element. To my utter lack of surprise, they too were full of thorium.
cues.zh: 手环那个事情，我看到有人辩称粉尘风险微乎其微，但别逗了。把这玩意儿绑在脸上，整晚慢悠悠地吸着粉尘，或者弄进眼睛里，这怎么可能没事。我做了和上次完全一样的测试，先用盖革计数器检测，再用伽马能谱仪确定元素。毫无意外，这里面也全是钍。

cues.en: However, what was interesting was I picked up a bracelet from the same company and it was totally empty, not even a trace of radiation,
cues.zh: 不过有趣的是，我从同一家公司买了一条手环，里面竟然空空如也，连一点辐射痕迹都没有，

cues.en: which is awesome because now instead of actively polluting its customer's environment with radioactive dust, they've instead just committed fraud by claiming a bracelet releases ions when they definitely don't and is just a piece of silicon. Moving on from the eye mask, there's another company called Numi that makes the Numi card.
cues.zh: 这倒挺好，因为他们现在不会再用放射性粉尘污染顾客的环境了，而是改成了欺诈：声称手环能释放离子，其实根本不能，它就只是一块硅胶。说完眼罩，再来看看另一家公司 Numi，他们做了一款叫 Numi card 的产品。

cues.en: It's this conference badge looking thing that even came with a lanyard, but wow is this thing radioactive.
cues.zh: 就是这玩意儿，长得像会议胸牌，甚至还配了挂绳，但天哪，这东西有放射性。

cues.en: I have a fair collection of radioactive samples, and this thing is one of the hotter items in my collection.
cues.zh: 我收藏了不少放射性样品，而这东西是我收藏里辐射较强的物品之一。

cues.en: The only thing spicier than this is a piece of uranium glazed pottery called Fiestaware,
cues.zh: 唯一比它更“辣”的，是一块叫 Fiestaware 的铀釉陶器，

cues.en: which maxes out at about 12 per hour. The NuMe card hits a toasty 5.3 microsieverts per hour, which is about five times as radioactive as even the hottest bracelet.
cues.zh: 它的辐射最高约每小时12。而这张 NuMe 卡能达到热乎乎的每小时5.3微西弗，辐射强度约是最“辣”手链的五倍。

cues.en: Though the eye mask was still a nice toasty 2.4.
cues.zh: 虽然眼罩的温度还是很舒服的 2.4 度。

cues.en: What I found really terrifying was that when you go to the NuMe card website,
cues.zh: 我觉得真正吓人的是，你去 NuMe Card 的网站时，

cues.en: one of their other products is the Numi patch.
cues.zh: 会发现他们的另一款产品叫 Numi Patch。

cues.en: This to me implies that it's something you stick onto yourself and God knows what's in it and what it's leaching into the user's body. Now I need to make something very clear. Handling something like this for short periods of time is actually absolutely safe.
cues.zh: 在我看来，这东西是贴在身上的，天知道里面有什么，又会渗出什么进入使用者体内。现在我得把话说清楚：短时间接触这种东西其实绝对安全。

cues.en: Even a few hours of exposure won't hurt you as long as none of the dust from these items ends up in your lungs.
cues.zh: 即便暴露几个小时也不会对你有伤害，只要这些物品上的粉尘没有吸进肺里就行。

cues.en: The radiation itself isn't strong enough at these levels to hurt you from short exposures. You're at no higher risk of cancer from handling this for a few minutes than anyone else.
cues.zh: 在这样的辐射水平下，短时间接触并不会造成伤害。仅仅把玩几分钟，你患癌的风险并不会比其他人更高。

cues.en: However,
cues.zh: 然而，

cues.en: when the designed purpose of the thing is to be worn twenty four seven, three hundred and sixty five days a year, you start getting into the danger zone.
cues.zh: 当这件物品的设计初衷是让你一年 365 天、全天候 24 小时佩戴时，你就开始步入危险区了。

cues.en: Especially if that radioactive dust gets inside you, which seems likely when you're literally strapping it to your face.
cues.zh: 尤其是这些放射性粉尘进入体内时，毕竟你是真的把它绑在脸上，这种情况很可能发生。

cues.en: Interestingly,
cues.zh: 有意思的是，

cues.en: this is actually the same reason why uranium glazed pottery like I showed before is actually remarkably safe even though it's more radioactive.
cues.zh: 这其实也正是我之前展示的那种铀釉陶器虽然辐射更强，却相当安全的原因。

cues.en: The uranium is well contained in the glaze, so as long as it doesn't chip or fracture, it's totally safe to handle.
cues.zh: 铀被牢牢封在釉层里，只要釉面不崩裂或碎裂，拿在手里就完全安全。

cues.en: My piece was cut before it was sent to me, so I keep it in a plastic bag to contain any dust.
cues.zh: 我的这件寄给我之前就被切割过，所以我一直把它放在塑料袋里，防止粉尘散出来。

cues.en: But an intact piece of Fiesta ware is totally safe to drink out, for example, as long as it's intact.
cues.zh: 不过一件完好的 Fiesta 餐具用来喝水是完全安全的，比如，只要它完好无损。

cues.en: The reason the negative ion stuff is dangerous is exposure time is much higher than a dinner plate, and the dust is uncontained and sheds easily, or worse still,
cues.zh: 负离子那些东西之所以危险，是因为接触时间比餐盘长得多，而且粉尘不受控、很容易脱落，更糟的是，

cues.en: pure powdered radioactive material is contained in the items and is easy enough to release by accident,
cues.zh: 物品中含有纯粉末状放射性物质，很容易意外释放出来，

cues.en: which does make it a bit funny when schools get evacuated from a kid bringing in a piece of Fiesta wear. Unless they throw in a wood chipper and have the rest of their classmates line up in front of the output, it's actually a pretty safe item to show off if you're careful not to smash it. Radiation isn't a boogeyman. You just need to understand the risks and dangers.
cues.zh: 所以当学校因为一个孩子带来一件 Fiesta 餐具而疏散时，确实有点好笑。除非他们把它扔进碎木机，再让其他同学在出口前排好队，否则只要你小心别打碎它，这其实是个相当安全的展示品。辐射不是什么妖魔鬼怪。你只需要了解其中的风险和危险。

cues.en: Generally, keeping to short exposures within dose limits and making sure there's no dust and you're safe, which is why I tend to make fun of shows like Chernobyl which tend to get that very, very wrong. But it's also why the negative ion products should be avoided and ideally just not sold. They violate all of those rules.
cues.zh: 通常，只要把暴露时间控制在剂量限值内，确保没有粉尘、做好防护就行了。这也是我经常调侃《切尔诺贝利》这类剧的原因，它们在这方面常常错得离谱。负离子产品也因此应该避免使用，最好干脆别卖。它们违反了所有这些原则。

cues.en: They're inherently dusty and are meant to be worn for extended periods of time. So what do we do about this? Well, the great thing is, like I said, the NRC takes all of this very seriously.
cues.zh: 它们本身就容易产生粉尘，而且设计上要长时间佩戴。那该怎么办呢？好在，正如我所说，NRC 非常认真地对待这些问题。

cues.en: So when you go onto the NRC website, there's this giant report a concern button near the top of the page.
cues.zh: 当你打开 NRC 网站时，页面顶部附近有一个很醒目的“反映问题”按钮。

cues.en: This brings you to another page where there's a selection of things that you can do. Personally, what I suggest is emailing their allegations department.
cues.zh: 点击后会跳转到另一个页面，里面有几个选项可选。我个人建议是直接发邮件给他们的举报指控部门。

cues.en: Now, obviously, you don't wanna spam their inbox, and please don't do that. But writing a simple professional letter with as much detail about the items question is the best way to go about it. In my case, I'll be writing to them about the NuMe card and Energy Armor and outlining exactly what I found. I'll include the Geiger countermeasures and the results of the gamma spectroscopy as well as links to the products themselves.
cues.zh: 当然，大家千万别去狂轰滥炸他们的邮箱，请一定不要这么做。最好的做法是写一封简明、专业的邮件，尽可能详细地提供相关物品的信息。就我而言，我会写信反映 NuMe 卡和 Energy Armor 的情况，并详细列出我的发现。我会附上盖革计数器的测量数据、伽马能谱分析的结果，以及这些产品本身的链接。

cues.en: Once you file a complaint, someone from the department will reach out. In my case, when I was contacted after the last video went out, I got on a phone call with the fantastic ladies in the allegation department and explained the situation.
cues.zh: 一旦你提交了投诉，该部门就会有人跟进。拿我来说，上一期视频发布后有人联系了我，我和申诉部门几位非常棒的女士通了电话，说明了情况。

cues.en: I then provided all the information I just explained and was then sent a letter via email with the contents of my claim and what they were going to do about it. Basically, it said that they'd be contacting each of the companies and sellers and would send me another letter in thirty days once they've made their decisions and contacted the companies. Sure enough, thirty days later, another letter arrived detailing the results, which in this case was banning several companies from selling their products in The US. Now to be clear, not all radioactive items are banned for sale on the consumer market, just ones deemed frivolous by the NRC.
cues.zh: 随后我提供了刚才提到的全部信息，之后收到了一封电子邮件，里面列出了我的申诉内容以及他们打算采取的措施。基本上就是说，他们会联系涉事的每家公司和卖家，并在做出决定且联系完这些公司后的 30 天内再给我发一封信。果不其然，30 天后我又收到了一封信，详细说明了处理结果，这次是禁止了几家公司在美国销售其产品。需要说明的是，并非所有放射性物品都被禁止在消费市场销售，只有被 NRC 认定为非必要的才会被禁。

cues.en: So the radioactive material must serve a purpose. It can't just be haphazard.
cues.zh: 所以放射性材料必须有实际用途，不能随便乱来。

cues.en: So thoriated welding rods are allowed, but thorium laced underwear,
cues.zh: 所以钍钨焊条是允许的，但含钍内裤，

cues.en: not so much. And yes, those were some of the items we looked at in the last video. By the time this video goes out, I'll have filed a new complaint with them about the new items as well as a few stragglers I found on Amazon.
cues.zh: 就不太行了。没错，这些正是我们在上期视频中查看过的部分物品。等这期视频发布时，我已经就这些新物品以及我在亚马逊上发现的几个漏网之鱼，向他们提交了新的投诉。

cues.en: But if you find products like these, you're absolutely encouraged to write in, not just to the NRC, but whatever your local regulatory commission is in your country.
